notes.text: Elmer Söderblom is out week to week (upper body injury) and has missed the last 9 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Rutger McGroarty has taken his spot beside Connor Dewar and Blake Lizotte.
Evgeni Malkin is out, reported after he played in their last game. He is a top-six forward.

Bryan Rust is on injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 11 games. Tommy Novak has taken his spot beside Sidney Crosby and Rickard Rakell. That line has had 58% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 66:42 together, up from 43% with Rust.
Trevor van Riemsdyk returned in their last game after missing 15 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
Ilya Solovyov has started killing penalties: on the ice for 43% of the team’s shorthanded time in 3 games, up from 5% last season.
Nick Robertson has started killing penalties: on the ice for 30% of the team’s shorthanded time in 20 games, up from 2% with his old team last season.
Konsta Helenius is on injured reserve (upper body injury) and has missed the last 10 games.
Zach Metsa has started killing penalties: on the ice for 28% of the team’s shorthanded time in 18 games, up from 7% last season.

story.head: Strength in numbers for the Penguins
paras: The Penguins (7-12-2) lost 5-2 to St. Louis on Nov 19, while the Sabres (9-9-4) beat Washington 6-3 the same night. Going in, the Pens are last in the Metropolitan (tied for 28th in the NHL) and the Sabres sixth in the Atlantic (tied for 20th).

The Penguins have played better than their record (.381) says: their chances are worth about .538, and their finishing has held them back. The Sabres’ record (.500) is about what their chances are worth.
This season, the Sabres have been outscored 76-64, but only 46-43 at 5-on-5. On special teams, opponents have outscored them 23-13.

The Penguins sit back rather than chase on the forecheck (lowest), get more of their shots from in close than anyone (1st) and rarely throw hits (lowest). On the other side, the Sabres rarely get pinned in their own end (3rd) and get their defensemen shooting (5th), but don’t block many shots (30th). The Penguins roll four lines, but the Sabres lean on their top six. On top of that, the Penguins could find some good looks against the Sabres, who give up plenty of them.

Erik Karlsson (3 G / 16 A / 19 P in 21 GP) leads the Penguins in scoring, and Tommy Novak (8 G / 7 A / 15 P in 21 GP) has a team-high eight goals. For the Sabres, Tage Thompson (14 G / 10 A / 24 P in 22 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Jack Quinn (11 G / 11 A / 22 P in 22 GP) isn’t far behind.

Pittsburgh has two options in net: Artūrs Šilovs (5-7-1 / .873 SV% in 13 GS) and Sergei Murashov (2-5-1 / .893 SV% in 8 GS). Šilovs has started six of their last ten games, including the last one on Nov 19. Buffalo also has two options: Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen (6-4-3 / .872 SV% in 12 GS) and Alex Lyon (0-2-1 / .898 SV% in 3 GS). Luukkonen has started four of their last ten games, including the last one on Nov 19. For both teams, it’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
